title: One column
rule: Ten or more wide, shallow panels stacked in a single column, read top to bottom like a storyboard.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: ten storyboard boards, each a 1894 x 222 px strip of cream card, stacked in one column with 40 px gutters; board numbers 1-10 in graphite in the left gutter; a punched hole at each board's corner

AGENT and STRANGER as the engraving puppets of page 03 (films/swarm/99-ways/kit/build_page03.py: the 1863 telegraph operator cut at the joints and pinned with brass pins; the 1867 hatted woman cut along a drawn path; the operator's table from the same plate), printed as ink on cream card, re-posed per board; the woman is seen only head-and-shoulders THROUGH the ticket window (scale 0.42, laid into the opening and cut off at the sill, no pin), facing the agent in boards 4-6 and turned away in board 7

the ticket window drawn in the shared pen hand: a pale cool platform wash with the platform edge beyond the glass, frame, cross glazing bars and white glass glints drawn OVER her, a sill ledge and a counter front lettered TICKET OFFICE

set in the shared pen hand (HANDMADE): memo with the canon text, a large wall clock with all sixty minute ticks set to each board's time (4:08 in board 1, 4:09 in boards 2-5, 4:10 from board 6; at 4:10 the minute hand sits on the two-o'clock mark, at 4:09 one tick short), cupboard hinged on the left jamb with the key on its hook and SERVICE tag, SERVICE door lettered SERVICE, TICKET OFFICE on the window
the four canon lines as cut-paper balloons in the shared pen hand (penlib.balloon_piece); ten torn commentary slips pinned with brass pins (build_page03.slip)

events.board 1: E0: 4:08. The memo on his desk.
events.board 3: E0: He sets off for the cupboard.
events.board 4: E1: On his way, a lady at the window.
events.board 5: E2: He looks up at the clock.
events.board 7: E3: She thanks him and goes.
events.board 9: E4: He opens the cupboard: the key.
events.board 10: E5: The key stays. The door stays shut.

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the boards are pinned down the single column one after another, so the story is read as a camera tilting down a storyboard
beat_frames: b01: boards 1-2 pinned down the column (board 2: E0)
b02: boards 1-4 pinned down the column (board 4: E1)
b03: boards 1-6 pinned down the column (board 6: E2)
b04: boards 1-7 pinned down the column (board 7: E3)
b05: boards 1-9 pinned down the column (board 9: E4)
b06: boards 1-10 pinned down the column (board 10: E5)

self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
self_check.evidence: measured (size, pixel checks named in the repair) and judged from the full-size page by the repair maker; a fresh blind reading of the repair is pending

weaknesses: at 222 px board height the puppets are about 200 px tall: small at phone width, legible at full size
board 1 is still a close-up (memo, hand, clock at 4:08) with much empty card
one minute is a single tick on the dial: 4:09 and 4:10 are told apart only by whether the minute hand sits on the 2 mark or one tick short; legible at full size, not at phone width
the engraved window piece of the 1863 plate is no longer used; the window is pen-drawn so the glass can sit in front of her

changed: clock redrawn larger (r 56 px) with all sixty minute ticks, set per board: 4:08 in board 1 (clock now shown there), 4:09 in boards 2-5, 4:10 from board 6

the stranger is seen head-and-shoulders through a pen-drawn ticket window: platform wash behind her, her puppet laid into the opening and cut off at the sill (no pin on her), frame, cross glazing bars and white glints drawn over her; counter front lettered TICKET OFFICE
she faces the agent in boards 4-6 and is turned away in board 7
board 4 question balloon set in three lines to the right of the window, tail to the window's edge (off her head); board 6 answer balloon moved low so its tail passes under her face
repairs.pass_test: every board's clock agrees with its caption time, and her face is visible behind the glass in boards 4-7
